01 / The first finger

A body is a better tutorial
than a control diagram.

The athlete starts above the court holding a basketball. A hand prompt asks for a jump. In the air, holding the screen brings the body into a tuck; releasing extends it. The same finger both asks for more style and decides when style must stop.

The launch is not a free aiming gesture. The route supplies a broad direction, and the player works within its travel time. This reduces the number of things a novice must learn while keeping a meaningful timing problem: an extra revolution is valuable only if the athlete can still make the next contact.

The official instructions confirm the three actions. The pictures explain their consequences more effectively: the ball never becomes a separately aimed projectile, and the moving athlete is the tool. A web adaptation should preserve that ownership. Replacing it with a drag-to-aim ball shot would change the central decision. Official control description.

The route gives time. The finger spends it.

Qualitative relationship. A trampoline renews the opportunity; a slide carries the body into a different kind of approach; a portal changes the scene while the attempt continues. No source frame establishes a universal release window in milliseconds.

02 / The price of another spin

Greed lives between
two safe poses.

Landing and progression are related, but they are not the same achievement.

A clean dunk closes the physical attempt. The flip target asks whether that successful attempt was ambitious enough. This allows a familiar course to remain useful after the player has learned where it goes.

The hard moments are local: stop spinning before a pad, use its rebound to start another rotation, and stop again before the rim. A long chain is several commitments under one result. The whole attempt remains at risk, so a late error has more emotional weight than an early one.

Failure also carries comedy. The athlete collapses near the court instead of becoming an abstract red cross. That feedback gives the player a bodily explanation—until the pose clips through the floor or a generic message obscures the cause.

The best retry lets the player say:
“I know what to change this time.”

For mobile web, preserve the contact pose briefly, name the actionable error, and restore the same route. A generic “Unlucky” label has personality but gives little help with the next release. Avoid reproducing clipping as a feature.

03 / A small verb, a large course grammar

The environment edits
the rhythm of the finger.

Pads, slides and portals are valuable because they change when the player must stop or restart a flip. A new backdrop alone cannot do that work.

Four functional families

Perches and drops introduce airborne time and a destination. Boxes, balconies and rooftops reuse this opening with different height and context.

Rebound relays break a long flight into contact problems. Trampolines on cars, aircraft and other props give those problems memorable silhouettes.

Carried motion uses flumes and curved slides to connect jumps. A good adaptation makes the exit direction readable before asking for the next spin.

Transitions and spectacle place portals, elaborate scenery and breakable backboards around the core action. Their reveal is a reason to continue, while their gameplay role must remain clear.

The records also show cannons, siege machinery and animals. A still can establish their presence; it cannot establish their attack cycle, collision damage or timing formula. Treat a prop as scenery until its functional rule is evidenced or explicitly designed.

04 / Two kinds of completion

A dunk closes the jump.
A target opens the next one.

Three jobs for the result screen

It celebrates the dunk, explains how the flip count maps to milestones, and offers another attempt or the next course. Those jobs should be resolved in that order. If a progression requirement is discovered only after the dunk, an apparently good outcome can feel unexpectedly invalid.

The early result uses a one-flip key tier and a two-flip coin tier. Its coin grant animates; its Continue padlock is temporary in the inspected sequence. The later rooftop has a three-tier ladder. These are course-specific examples, not a universal pricing or progression formula.

Key imagery connects performance to another reward system, but the complete key-to-box flow is not visible here. Preserve that uncertainty when describing the original. In the target, give every reward a defined purpose and tell the player that purpose before collecting it.

Advancement should be forecast. Put the required flip count beside the current count before launch and during flight. Keep extra medal goals subordinate. A player should understand why a safe dunk can still invite Retry.

05 / Content and renewal

The next world is a reveal.
The next route is a test.

The recognizable athlete and basketball survive radical changes of scale and setting. That continuity makes portals and absurd platforms feel like variations of the same game.

Worlds are not necessarily equal chapters or unique level sets. The visible progression reaches Level 100, while a familiar city court appears at Level 90. The early and late city views support recurrence, but they do not establish an exact repeat period. The adaptation should finish an authored campaign visibly, then offer replay and mastery without pretending a repeated route is newly discovered content.

06 / Feedback that survives the stunt

Style needs a readable
physical consequence.

Flip callouts, orange trails and praise words keep long flights from becoming silent waiting. They should stay away from the upcoming contact point. The same attention budget must accommodate the athlete’s angle, the next pad, and the flip requirement. A spectacular overlay that hides any of these weakens the timing game it is celebrating.

The camera sells height and motion by keeping a large athlete in the foreground and sending surfaces through depth. Close creator zooms sometimes obscure the next destination; those recording edits are not a prescription for the target camera. Preserve visibility of the next contact and let the celebration expand only after contact has been resolved.

07 / Rewards and interruptions

A bonus should renew play.
A coin should have a job.

The source is free with ads and in-app purchases. Failure screens expose an ad-marked Skip; a bonus invite exposes another video icon. Their completed ad flows and reward settlement are not inspected. A storefront listing for No Ads is not proof that the recorded player bought it.

Coin utility varies across the available versions. The old footage does not show a shop, and some dated player reviews describe stockpiling coins without a sink. The current iOS listing offers coin purchases; later reviews describe cosmetics. The browser host instead describes coins as points. These statements belong to different products or builds. Current mobile offers · browser coin explanation.

For bug.games, use a clear earned medal ladder and free chapter rewards. Do not reproduce a balance whose spending system is unknown. A bonus route should be unlocked by play and revisitable from the course map. Optional cosmetics may extend expression after the core game works; they must never purchase a clean landing or escape a progression wall.

08 / Market and reception

The promise lands.
The long tail needs purpose.

The strongest reception signal is a satisfying, understandable stunt. The recurring concerns are interruptions, repetition and broken continuation.

Google Play lists 4.7/5, 58.7K reviews and 10M+ downloads in its header at this snapshot. The US App Store shows 4.7/5 from 139K ratings. These are platform aggregates with different populations, not retention, revenue or unique active-player counts. Android listing · iOS listing.

Selected dated feedback is mixed: an iOS reviewer on 26 October 2021 praises variety and the match between advertising and play; Android feedback on 5 February 2023 raises unused coins and recurring layouts, while feedback on 27 May 2025 criticizes ad load. These are useful hypotheses from individual players, not a measured consensus.

Editorial review

The OnlineGames.io editor’s review, updated 14 May 2026, describes discovering real timing control beneath the spectacle and returning for more levels. It praises comic failures and portals. It provides no aggregate critic score.

No matching Steam listing or Metacritic/OpenCritic record was verified in the focused search. Similarly named Wii and PC games are separate products and supply no score for this mobile game.

09 / Visual and sonic direction

Keep the court clear.
Let the world be excessive.

The source hierarchy is consistent: a purple athlete, orange ball, large pad or rim, and bright praise. Courts and distant scenery can be busy because the athlete and contact surfaces keep distinctive shapes. White court markings explain where the ordinary game belongs; improbable props explain why this version is worth playing.

A mobile adaptation should keep the athletic silhouette large enough to read a tuck, a foot-first contact and an extension at a glance. Use bright pads against quieter scenery, a depth shadow to explain surface height, and camera anticipation toward the next destination. Do not solve visibility with a permanently drawn trajectory that gives away every timing decision.

The original sound’s timbre, music pulse and mix have not been audibly verified. The target audio brief therefore serves the action: a short launch lift, a rising flip accent, a pad rebound, a decisive dunk impact, and a softer failure cue followed by immediate readiness. Its detailed event sheet is a designed specification, not an assertion of exact source audio.

A funny fall can end an attempt.
A clear fall can improve the next one.
10 / Adaptation thesis

Keep the airborne bargain.
Make the career legible.

A complete web game can use fewer explicitly authored courses than the source’s visible level counter while preserving its meaningful variety. The target below specifies 42 distinct routes, seven chapters, three free coaster detours and a mastery finish.

The count is a design decision, not a reconstructed count of source layouts. Every chapter contains a new contact problem, a combination route and a finale. Replay remains available after finishing. Earned looks and best medals give the career a purpose without obscuring the act of jumping.

The transfer priorities are narrow: a launch the player understands, continuous risk from extra flips, distinct travel apparatus, visible contact feedback, and a result that explains advancement. Preserve those relationships. Design the missing constants and reward flows deliberately, then validate their consequences in play.

Readable implementation contract

Build layer

Ready as a complete-game specification with named source limits. The game itself has not been created, tested or submitted.

All figures are embedded below or above in this same file. Static text, tables and the prompt remain readable without scripts. Images are reference evidence; they are not licensed production assets. A receiving model must inspect the specified figures if it can decode images, and explicitly name any image-access limitation instead of implying visual access.

A / Short game-specific prompt

Build the entire stunt career

Build a complete original mobile web flip-and-dunk game from this Hoop World 3D teardown. Use #build-rules and the 42-course catalogue: seven free chapters, three unlockable coaster detours, bronze/silver/gold mastery, replay, a real campaign finish and device saves. Tap launches; airborne hold rotates; release extends and stops rotation for pad or rim contact. Preserve the extra-flip risk, chained rebounds, carried slide exits, portal reveals, bodily failure and satisfying dunk. Use original 2.5D art with depth, a readable athlete, orange ball and clear landing silhouettes; inspect the required embedded figures rather than reproducing screenshots. Source constants are unknown: implement the marked designed rules and tune them through the listed cases. Include complete EN/RU interface switching and separate saved Music/SFX sliders. Work standalone first, then conditionally integrate the current bug.games SDK lifecycle, native analytics, moments and guarded saves. The free game must remain whole if SDK, sign-in, network or optional cosmetics are unavailable. Follow the Extras contract; show only real approved offers and preserve owned entitlements. Return one portable game HTML plus the documented platform metadata when implementation is requested; do not build a short prototype.

C / Complete target rules — designed

The entire free game

Designed specification These constants define a coherent adaptation. They are starting values for tuning, not measurements of the source.

  1. State machine: BOOT → READY → AIR → CONTACT; valid pad contact returns to AIR, slide contact enters CARRIED then AIR, portal enters TRANSIT then AIR, valid final rim contact enters DUNK → RESULT. Invalid contact or leaving bounds enters FAIL → RESULT. RESULT offers Retry, map, and Continue if bronze is met. PAUSED overlays any active state without advancing its clock.
  2. Input: a primary pointerdown in READY launches and begins a hold. During AIR, held input tucks and rotates forward. Pointerup extends and decelerates rotation to zero over a designed 80 ms; the body does not snap automatically upright. Re-holding retucks. Use pointer capture; ignore secondary fingers and prevent scroll only on the play surface. Mouse and Space are optional equivalent controls. UI buttons consume their event.
  3. Travel: author each segment’s start, endpoint, duration, apex and contact type in world space. Sample a ballistic-like parabola for normal arcs, a spline for slides and a paired transform for portals. Orientation changes do not steer the route horizontally. Use a fixed 1/120 s simulation step with an accumulator; sweep contact volumes to prevent tunneling. Rendering can interpolate at 30/60 fps without changing outcomes.
  4. Rotation: begin at angle 0; hold rate 10 rad/s initially. Count a flip after each accumulated full forward revolution (2π), never from limb animation or a partial turn. Keep unwrapped angle separate from normalized contact angle. Count carries across pads and portals, not across attempts. Carried slide travel does not award flips; an airborne launch resumes normal counting.
  5. Contact: pad success requires feet in its landing volume, downward approach and body angle within ±40° of feet-first; the next arc starts once. Rim success requires descending ball entry, hands/ball presented, extended pose and angle within ±25° of upright. Everything else at a terminal surface fails. A near miss does not become an assisted dunk. Freeze invalid contact for 300 ms before presenting Retry; allow early dismissal after the visible impact.
  6. Reachability: base arc duration starts at 2.8 s and authored multi-segment routes may total 4–8.5 s of air time. Each route must prove its gold count feasible at the rotation rate with at least 250 ms of release allowance at each mandatory contact. Tune durations before lowering rules; the listed thresholds are design targets subject to this feasibility check. Camera changes cannot change simulation timing.
  7. Course result: bronze minimum M unlocks the next course only after a valid dunk. Silver needs M+1 flips; gold M+2. A dunk under M is a landed attempt with “One more flip needed” or its plural equivalent, no advancement, and Retry. Best medal and best successful flip count are monotonic per course. Failed attempts award no medal; retry never costs progress.
  8. Scenery and mechanisms: pads are functional; vehicle decks follow deterministic paths restarted with each attempt; flumes lock the carried pose until a visible exit; portals retain count and map orientation through their paired bases. Glass/boards fragment decoratively after a permitted trigger. Animal and dragon silhouettes are scenery by default, with no hidden damage. Late cannon courses use an explicitly designed warned obstacle, not an assumed source attack rule.
  9. Fever: at the fourth full flip in an attempt, add a short callout and an orange trail. The trail is capped, stays behind the body, and changes neither rate nor tolerance. Reduced-effects mode removes the trail and glass shower while keeping count and outcome labels. Reset the streak on Retry, fail or finished result.
  10. Career: seven chapters of six courses in a fixed order. A chapter opens after bronze on its predecessor’s finale. Course map permits replay of every unlocked route; the active first-unfinished course is highlighted. Give free outfit variants at 8, 24 and 42 bronze clears. Base jersey, ball, trails-off choice and all gameplay are free. No coin balance, stamina, health upgrades, subscription or daily obligation.
  11. Bonuses and finish: unlock B1 after C06, B2 after W06 and B3 after I06. Each coaster route has its own best-medal record and can be entered repeatedly without spending tickets; the ticket icon means access, not a consumable balance. Bonus failure returns to its start and cannot block the campaign. After K06 bronze, show “Career complete”, 42-course medal summary, Replay and remaining mastery; all 42 golds give a distinct Master finish. No infinite fake level numbering.
  12. Assistance: after three consecutive failures on the same course, offer free Practice at 0.8 simulation speed. Clearly mark it before launch; it can teach the route and records practice completion separately, with no competitive gold. Return to normal play in one tap. Unlocking the next normal course still uses its disclosed bronze rule. Tune the first six courses to avoid needing Practice routinely.
  13. Errors and saves: checkpoint after settled result and chapter unlock, not every animation frame. Reload restores course, medals, unlocks and settings and starts READY at the saved course; never reconstruct half a failed flight or issue another reward from a resumed result animation. Input cancels on focus loss, orientation change or settings entry.

E / The first 20 minutes — intended pacing

Teach one action, then ask for a choice

CheckpointPlayer experienceCompletion signal
0–30 secondsOpen C01 directly. A context prompt teaches launch, hold and release. A modest camera move reveals rim and landing; no reward modal or purchase panel before first action.First launch and first resolved attempt. A clean contact is attainable with one deliberate flip.
2 minutesC02/C03 establish a pad rebound and a required count. The player sees a failure cause, retries the same setup and learns that gold is optional.At least one successful retry and an understood bronze gate; progress pace is a tuning target, not a guarantee.
5 minutesApproach or finish City; first relay finale and optional B1 ticket. Let the next airfield reveal follow the City result.Chapter progress is clear; declining B1 continues the campaign without lost reward.
10 minutesAircraft/Waterway routes introduce carried travel and portals; an earned look becomes available after eight bronze clears.At least one return to a known course for a better medal, or clear forward progression.
20 minutesA skilled player may be near the career finish; others may still be in later chapters. Map, free Practice and saves support both. Remaining medals and three detours provide return goals.Player can state the next objective, find an earlier route and resume later. No forced daily loop.

Most target attempts should resolve in roughly 5–15 seconds of active play, plus a brief readable result. These are designed pacing goals to measure during implementation. Edited videos do not certify real session length or retention.

G / Mobile interface, language and audio settings

EN/RU and independent volumes are game requirements

The report is English. The future game must switch its complete interface between EN and RU in Settings from READY, pause and result screens. Switching changes labels, tutorial, course names, failure advice, medal requirements and Extras copy immediately; it must not restart the career or current course. First boot may choose a supported browser language, with English fallback; a saved explicit choice wins afterwards. Source iOS lists Russian support, but this exact target UI and slider behavior are newly designed.

A specification of the future interface, not a playable settings panel in this report.

  • Use separate Music and SFX gain buses. Initial target defaults: music 35%, SFX 70%, stored per device on change with a short debounce. Zero must be true silence on that bus; music at zero must leave pad/dunk cues audible, and SFX at zero must leave music unchanged.
  • Effective bus gain = saved user level × platform mute gate × pause/visibility gate. A platform mute never overwrites user sliders; unmute restores prior levels. Resume AudioContext only after a trusted player gesture. Settings previews are optional and must obey platform mute.
  • Portrait 9:16 is primary; safe-area insets, no sideways scrolling. At 390×844 use at least 44 CSS-pixel hit targets and place actions clear of the athlete/rim. On landscape, keep a centered playfield and readable HUD, with no new input mechanic.
  • Top HUD: course, current flips and required M, pause. Bottom actions appear only in READY/result. A result names Dunk / Need more flips / Bad contact, highlights the affected surface and exposes Retry immediately. Continue becomes active only after progress is settled.
  • RU must fit without shrinking text below readable sizes. Use proper singular/plural forms for flips and course progress; avoid text baked into images. Keyboard focus, visible state labels and reduced effects support accessible operation.
H / Audio and motion contract

Event timing serves contact and readiness

Source fidelity unverified Game audio has not been heard through an audio-capable inspection tool. The input includes images and textual descriptions; browser sequence inspection does not establish timbre, tempo, layering or mix. Every cue below is designed, currently missing as a production asset. Planned filenames are identifiers, not delivered files. Procedural or newly licensed assets may fill them in implementation; no paid service or copied source audio is required.

Trigger / planned assetDesigned cue and motion roleMix / readiness
Launch
sfx/launch		Short cloth/body whoosh with a low spring lift; coincide with leaving READY. Brief anticipation in the torso, no long control lock.Medium priority, one per attempt. Input is already live; cue must not gate the flight.
Full revolution
sfx/flip		Light rising tick and air accent on each full 2π count; small counter pulse near athlete. Subtle alternating variation prevents a repeated identical burst.Low priority; cap overlapping voices. Dunk/pad may interrupt it. No extra cue for a partial turn.
Valid pad contact
sfx/pad		Soft compression plus bright rebound; synchronized pad squash and next-arc launch.High contact priority, short recovery. Next hold remains live. Do not play if the contact failed.
Slide exit / portal
sfx/slide, sfx/portal		Quiet carried rush; short tonal swell for transition, resolving at visible exit. No full-screen flash.Duck music slightly for portal, not the next contact cue. Preserve orientation/count during TRANSIT.
Dunk / board break
sfx/dunk, sfx/glass		Solid rim thump plus net swish; decorative crack only on board/glass events. Body extends, rim flexes, camera gives one small impulse.Highest gameplay priority. Settle result once; celebration may continue while Retry/Continue becomes usable.
Invalid contact
sfx/fail		Muted bump and brief comic fall accent; maintain the impact pose for designed 300 ms.Lower loudness than dunk. No mocking long fanfare; Retry is reachable immediately after the short hold.
Fever / medal / chapter finish
sfx/streak, sfx/medal, sfx/chapter		Short upward flourish for streak; one resolving motif for earned medal; a fuller version for chapter finish.Play only on state transition / newly improved medal. No stacked fanfares for all prior tiers on every replay.

Music brief: an original light percussive sports loop with a compact bass pulse, sparse bright melodic accents and ample space for contact sounds. City is the baseline; sky opens the arrangement; marine/cavern use restrained, darker texture; castle adds a finish lift. Bonus coaster can be slightly busier. No source BPM or exact instrumentation is asserted. Author loop-safe phrase boundaries, short crossfades at chapter changes, and a result sting that does not restart the entire score after every attempt. Music pauses or fades under platform pause, and resumes in phase without audible clicks. Assets for all contexts are missing until produced/licensed and verified.

Motion validation: record normal-speed target traces of launch→flip→release→pad and final rim contact. Compare silhouette, camera look-ahead, sense of height and input response against tuck, extension, pad and slam. The independently inspected source still sequence supports pose order; edited creator footage does not calibrate an exact rotation rate, rebound coefficient or animation duration.

I / bug.games integration plan

Base play survives platform absence

Contract checked against the connected bug.games SDK documentation on 5 October 2026. This is an integration plan, not an implemented connection. The SDK is an optional platform layer around a working single-player game. Recheck its current documentation at implementation time.

  1. Guarded bootstrap: standalone mode runs immediately. If window.parent === window, stay local before attempting the platform import. In an embedded frame, conditionally import /sdk/bloomplay.js, check bloomplay.isEmbedded, then initialize with a bounded timeout. Distinguish ordinary standalone from initialization failure; neither may leave BOOT permanently spinning. Call platform loaded only when the actual first interaction is ready.
  2. Lifecycle: call gameplayStart() and gameplayStop() at READY→AIR and the terminal result or real pause, not at each intermediate pad/portal state or in a frame loop. The whole attempt remains active through CONTACT, CARRIED, TRANSIT and DUNK. If the SDK connects late, synchronize the current state once. Handle onPause reasons including hidden, sign-in, purchase and dialog. Freeze clocks and clear held inputs idempotently; onResume returns to an explicit Tap to resume overlay. Never advance a hidden attempt by elapsed wall time.
  3. Audio: platform onMute / muted state gates both buses while preserving the two saved levels. Browser visibility/focus pauses also gate sound. Returning to the page restores levels only after intentional resume; gestures must not accidentally launch or rotate through the overlay.
  4. Progress save: begin local storage first. In platform mode use bloomplay.save, await its readiness and checkpoint through save.set. Keep schema version and monotonic best medals/counts/unlocks; merge by per-course maxima. Device language/volume belongs in a separate local preference key. A delayed cloud read cannot overwrite newer earned progress. Failed reads are not empty data.
  5. Services: no multiplayer, camera/microphone permission, authentication wall or server dependency is required for the base game. Platform analytics and moments supplement local play. No ad API is assumed; no revenue or sales result is asserted.

J / Native analytics and progress moments

Measure the decision, then the continuation

Use bloomplay.analytics.track(event, props) for explicit semantic transitions; it is fire-and-forget. No external tracking dependency, personal information or frame-by-frame stream is required. A local no-op adapter preserves standalone play. Event payloads use an attempt ID and stable course ID; deduplicate terminal events.

EventWhen / minimal propertiesQuestion it answers
attempt_startREADY→AIR: course, chapter, attempt number, practice flag, input kind.Do people reach the first action and retry?
attempt_endOne terminal outcome: dunk_pass / dunk_under_target / pad_fail / rim_fail / obstacle / bounds; flips, M, segment, active duration, medal, best improved.Which contact or requirement blocks progress?
retryResult→same READY: previous cause, course, attempts on course.Does a readable failure lead to another attempt?
course_clearFirst bronze only: course, chapter, attempts to clear, practice excluded.Where does the career slow down?
map_actionOpen / select replay / select next: from, target course.Are return goals understood?
bonus_actionOffer shown / enter / decline / finish: B1–B3, access unlock, no coin spending.Does the detour refresh the session?
practice_actionOffer / accept / leave: course and recent failures.Is learning assistance resolving friction?
settings_changeSetting name and coarse selected value; language en/ru, audio quartile, reduced effects.Are defaults useful? Never send typed text or device identifiers.
save_stateFailure / recovery / migration result and schema version, once per state change.Can continuation failures be separated from timing failures?
extra_actionIf enabled: visible approved offer / purchase start / result / owned selection; product ID, normalized result.Does an optional offer behave correctly? Never infer a sale from button click.

Moments: declare the seven metadata names and call bloomplay.progress.moment(name) at their real transitions. First corrected retry means a valid pass on the same course after a recorded failure; First gold means a gold medal once; chapter/career moments depend on settled saved progress. Restore a local “moments emitted” set across reload to avoid repeated calls; the platform moment API is write-only, so do not promise read-back achievements.

Readouts to inspect after launch: first launch → first result → first pass funnel; fail cause per segment; attempts-to-bronze distribution; Retry and Continue rate; active time to City completion; bonus entry/decline; map replay use; completion/return cohorts; save failure rate. Separate practice, new and returning players. Set numerical acceptance thresholds only after baseline data exists. Do not equate storefront ratings, edited-video enthusiasm or an arbitrary target percentage with retention.

K / Optional Extras — complete free base first

Sell expression only if an approved offer exists

Initial metadata uses products: []. No empty shop or dead Extras button is shown. A later optional plan may request two durable cosmetic products: Sunset Court Palette and Comet Trail Pack. They change scenery colours / a bounded trail, never tolerance, rotation, medals, chapter access or retry. A free baseline palette, base trail choice and earned outfits remain available.

Product declarations are requests for staff approval. Query monetization.getProducts() and render only real returned offers with their actual name, coin price and kind; a planned item is not sellable. Platform coins are separate from the omitted source coin wallet. Do not create a top-up flow, promise conversion to money or assume an ad reward can fund an Extra.

Catalogue / entitlement stateRequired behavior
Product returned, not ownedShow the actual approved offer with preview and explicit purchase action. Unavailable balance or cancellation cannot affect play.
Owned durable, present or removed from saleRead getEntitlements(); retain selection/use even if absent from current catalogue. Show Owned / Use, no second buy.
No products, offline or SDK absentHide purchase entry and keep all routes and free looks. Existing device-cached owned selections may remain available pending authoritative restoration.
Catalogue or entitlement read failedKeep previous ownership, avoid pretending it is empty, and offer a later retry from Settings. No game-blocking error.
Purchase succeedsAwait the real purchase result, refresh entitlement, grant/select once, checkpoint, close modal and return to paused state before explicit resume.
Cancelled / insufficient coins / failedNo grant, progress change or audio leak. Explain the result briefly and return to the same prior state.

Do not submit these offers during teardown authoring. Recheck the current SDK and staff requirements when a finished game is actually being published.

Whole-game completion gate: all 42 distinct course entries and three bonus routes exist; every required mechanism is used meaningfully; normal and Practice behavior are differentiated; no broken Continue; saved replay/finish works; both languages and both volume buses work; source/reference limits are not used to justify placeholder courses. Performance budget is designed: target 60 fps on a representative midrange phone, graceful 30 fps fallback, bounded particles and no remote asset requirement for base play.
